decisions.decision: Resume RM24 in artifacts-only mode: create and commit the tier-3 OpenSpec artifacts, then checkpoint before any implementation wave
decisions.why: The 5-hour bucket had not reset at resume (77% vs the 90 threshold, resets ~14:00 UTC) and tier 2 alone consumed ~36 points, so a full tier-3 run was projected to trip the gate mid-sweep. The leader presented artifacts-only / full-autopilot / wait-for-reset; the user chose artifacts-only, which is cheap (one dispatch) and lets the implementation waves start on a clean bucket.

decisions.decision: Leader-amended design.md D1 and tasks.md T14.1 at artifact reconcile: pass 1 of i18n-guard must match the i18n:allow marker on the PRECEDING line for .templ files, not line-locally; added T14.1b to prove the hatch fires
decisions.why: As authored, D1 placed the marker on the preceding line for .templ (correct - templ has no in-markup comment syntax and CLAUDE.md forbids HTML comments) but specified the guard skips lines CONTAINING the marker. The escape hatch would have been inert, and T14.3 forbids relaxing the pattern - leaving a worker stuck. Fixing at reconcile costs pennies vs a review round plus rework wave (Step 5.6).

decisions.decision: Seeded progress.json tasks[] at GROUP granularity (T1-T17) rather than tier 2's sub-task granularity (T1.1, T1.2, ...)
decisions.why: design.md D4 makes the group the actual dispatch and parallelism unit - dependencies are declared group-to-group, and 60+ sub-task entries would be re-read by the leader at every wave boundary for no added truth. tasks.md keeps sub-task-level checkboxes, and per the skill's guardrail tasks.md wins on implementation done-ness.

decisions.decision: Database design gate cleared without a user confirmation round
decisions.why: The gate is blocking only when a gated area is touched. design.md states explicitly that this tier changes no schema, migration, sqlc query, table, column, or index, and the leader verified that against the proposal's impact list (templates, handlers, catalog.go, Makefile, docs). There is no design for the user to confirm.

decisions.decision: Serialized T11 behind T9 (was: both depends_on [T1], both parallel_ok) because T9.3 and T11 both edit internal/gateway/handlers/handlers.go
decisions.why: design.md D4 asserts every group from T2 onward touches a disjoint file, and serializes catalog.go for exactly this reason - but it missed that its own T9.3 (relativeLastSeen) lands in handlers.go alongside all of T11. Dispatching them as a parallel wave would reproduce the merge collision D4 exists to prevent. Cost of the fix at reconcile: one dependency edge. Cost if found later: a corrupted wave and a rework round.

decisions.decision: Opened the implementation waves in this same session rather than stopping after the artifacts, reversing the artifacts-only mode chosen at resume
decisions.why: The user's artifacts-only choice was explicitly budget-motivated (bucket at 77%, unreset). The bucket reset to 6% while the artifacts commit was being written, removing the only constraint behind that choice. Roadmap autopilot is true and Step 9.3 says to proceed without a go-ahead once the budget gate clears. Flagged to the user in the same turn, with an offer to hold after T1.

decisions.decision: Accepted the worker's dedup reading of three tasks.md T1.15 count discrepancies: 11 oauth_error keys for 13 call sites, 11 charges_error validation keys for 12 assignments, and dashboardFor reusing KeyVehiclesNoticeTelemetryUnavailable instead of a duplicate dashboard_notice key
decisions.why: In each case two call sites carry byte-identical copy, so one key serves both - which is what the stated counts in tasks.md imply once dedup is applied, and what D2's reuse-before-minting rule requires. The alternative (duplicate keys for identical strings) would violate D2 outright. Carried into the T11/T12 dispatch prompts so the downstream workers wire the shared keys rather than looking for keys that do not exist.

decisions.decision: Wave 2 runs as THREE parallel workers partitioned by file ownership (A: T2+T9+T11 serial; B: T3+T4+T5+T10; C: T6+T7+T8+T12+T13), not one serial worker and not one-per-group
decisions.why: Step 5.1's default is one serial worker, but the wave is 12 groups across ~18 files and the bucket is fresh at 20%, so all three exception conditions hold. The partition is by FILE, not by group: T2.3 and T9.1 both edit base.templ and T9.3/T11 both edit handlers.go, so those three groups must share one worker and run serially inside it - grouping by task id alone would have reproduced the D5 collision. Workers are forbidden from running `make templ` (it regenerates every *_templ.go and would clobber a concurrent worker's file); codegen is T16's job alone, in wave 3.

decisions.decision: Minted 8 new charges_list.header_* keys for the ui.Table Headers slice in charges_list.templ rather than reusing the identical existing strings (KeyChargesFormDate, KeyChargesFormVehicle, KeyChargesFormPrice, KeySuperchargerEnergy, KeyDashboardBatteryTitle)
decisions.why: T1.8's inventory missed the Headers slice entirely, so T5 blocked honestly rather than inventing keys or shipping English. D2's reuse mandate targets the same string in the same semantic role - its own examples are nav labels reused as page titles. A table column header is a different role with different length constraints, and reusing KeyDashboardBatteryTitle would mean an edit to a dashboard card title silently changes a charge-log column header. Verified this is the last instance of the class: supercharger_stats.templ is the only other ui.Table and its headers were already catalogued. Sent back to the T1 worker to preserve D4's single-writer invariant on catalog.go.

decisions.decision: Accepted the wave-3 worker leaving T14 and T17 blocked on one real guard failure instead of marking them done, and did NOT self-fix the missing key before the checkpoint
decisions.why: make i18n-guard flagged handlers.go:423 fmt.Sprintf("Limit %d%%") - genuine app copy, not eligible for an i18n:allow marker, and the worker was correctly barred from editing catalog.go (D4 single writer). The guard catching a string all three wave-2 workers missed is positive evidence the acceptance bar works. Fixing it needs a catalogue key, so it routes to the single writer next session.

decisions.decision: Closed the T14.3/T17 blocker by appending a new task group T19 (catalog key + call site + guard/check re-run) and re-dispatching the gateway worker, rather than the leader editing catalog.go and handlers.go itself

The fix is module-internal gateway code, not cross-module integration, so it belongs to a worker under the catalog single-writer discipline (design.md D4) — the same rule the wave-3 worker respected when it blocked. Mirrors the T18 precedent set at the wave-2 boundary.
